markdown:
# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser sends polite payment reminders and collects the payment, for freelance designers, so they stop chasing late invoices by hand. Chaser is a working name, not fixed.

## Problem
Freelance designers hate asking for money. Today they keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. They lose a few hours a month on it.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer working alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or from a PDF. They want the money without asking for it. Hating the ask stops them.

## Core scenario
On a Monday morning at their desk, on a laptop, a designer sees an invoice two weeks overdue. They want to hand it to Chaser in under a minute and not think about it again until the money lands. It happens a few times a month.

## Also affected
The designer's clients, who get the reminders and pay through Chaser. They should feel nudged, not accused.

## Not for
- Agencies with a finance person.
- Freelancers outside design (developers, writers, consultants). We turn them away at sign-up.

## Feel
Calm, friendly, a bit dry.
Never pushy, corporate or cute.

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027. A paying user is any user on a paid plan, at any price.
2. $5,000 monthly revenue by the end of December 2027.

Earns by: See Open.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself.
2. No mobile app.

## Assumptions
Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name.

## Open
- Goals: Earns by is empty. Nothing says how Chaser makes money.
- Goals: No plan or price is set, so we cannot tell how many users $5,000 a month needs.
- Goals: Goal 2 does not say whether revenue means Chaser's own fees or the payments it collects for designers.
- Product: Chaser collects payment from the start, but how (methods, who holds the money) is not said.
- Anti-goals: Collecting payment pulls against "We will not build invoicing itself"; where one ends and the other starts is not said.
- Anti-goals: Neither anti-goal says why.
- Core scenario: How an invoice reaches Chaser (Wave, PDF, other) is not said.
- Not for: How sign-up tells a designer from another freelancer is not said.
- Assumptions: Nothing says how or when we will test the one assumption.

questions.question: Persona says brand or web designer, Not for says non-design is out: are illustrators, UX/product, motion and graphic designers in?
questions.why: Two readers would picture different users, and sign-up needs one line to turn people away or let them in.

questions.question: Do the client reminders speak as the designer, or as Chaser in its own voice?
questions.why: Feel (calm, a bit dry) is written for the designer, but clients read the emails, and dry can sound cold or like a collector.

questions.question: Does a designer who also does other work (dev, writing, consulting) or runs a small studio count as in or out?
questions.why: Not for says turn away at sign-up, but a mixed freelancer would be refused or admitted on a guess.
options: In if design is main work
In if they say they design

questions.question: How does Chaser earn: a subscription, a cut of each payment it collects, or both?
questions.why: Goal 2 cannot be checked, and Goal 1's "paid plan" has no meaning, until the earning model exists.

questions.question: Does the $5,000 in Goal 2 count Chaser's own revenue, or the total payments Chaser collects for designers?
questions.why: The two differ by 10x to 50x, so the same date would mean very different results.

questions.question: Where does collecting payment end and invoicing begin: does Chaser only send a pay link for an invoice the designer already made?
questions.why: Collecting payment pulls against "We will not build invoicing itself", and the line decides what the first version builds.
options: Pay link only, no invoice docs

questions.question: Why will Chaser not build invoicing, given that it already collects the payment?
questions.why: Without a reason, no one can tell whether a feature like a pay-link page, invoice templates or recurring billing counts as invoicing.
options: Wave and others do it well

questions.question: Will Chaser ever go past polite reminders, to late fees, collections or legal threats?
questions.why: It is the most tempting way to get paid faster, and it conflicts with the Feel and with clients feeling nudged, not accused.

questions.question: Does "No mobile app" still allow a phone-friendly web page where clients pay?
questions.why: Clients will often open reminders on a phone, so this decides whether mobile work for the pay page is in or out.
options: Yes, client web page is fine
Yes for both, as web only

questions.question: What evidence do you have that designers lose hours to chasing invoices and would pay to stop?
questions.why: The Problem rests on a claim with no source, and the whole product and both revenue goals depend on it being true.

questions.question: If designers refuse to let a tool email their clients in their name, what is the fallback?
questions.why: This is the one assumption that ends the product if false, and the document names no test or other route.
options: Give them a draft to send

questions.question: Why would a designer leave their spreadsheet and manual emails, or a free tool like Wave's own reminders, for Chaser?
questions.why: Wave and similar tools already send reminders, and the document names no alternative or reason to switch.
